clues.text: This launched steel coaster hits a top speed of 50 mph, reaches a height of 95 feet, and turns riders upside down through 3 inversions.
Manufactured by Premier Rides, this high-energy attraction officially opened to the public in 2010.
Riders flock to the state of Pennsylvania to experience this compact, airtime-filled launch coaster.
This coaster marked a major technical shift for its manufacturer as their first design to feature a linear synchronous motor (LSM) launch instead of linear induction motors.
The name of this ride evokes a classic festive firework launched high into the air, or a compound verb meaning to surge upward rapidly.

evidence.quote: Sky Rocket is a steel roller coaster located at Kennywood amusement park in West Mifflin, Pennsylvania.

Sky Rocket is an electromagnetic launch coaster using linear synchronous motors (LSM), a first for Premier Rides' designs. Premier Rides had previously only used linear induction motors (LIM) launches on their coasters.
The coaster did not have a name at the time of its announcement, but the park eventually decided on the name "Sky Rocket", after its ride model.
